THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Defendant Nos.2 and 3 in O.S.No.90/2008 on the file of the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge,
Bellary (hereinafter referred to as the 'Trial Court'), are impugning the judgment and decree dated 23.08.2011 decreeing the suit of the plaintiff holding that the plaintiff is entitled for damages of Rs.12,00,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of suit till realization and directing them to deposit the amount within 30 days from the date of the judgment.
2. The parties are referred to as per their ranks before the Trial Court.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the plaintiff filed the suit O.S.No.90/2008 against defendant Nos.1 to 4 claiming damages of Rs.24,88,600/- from the defendants with interest at 18% per annum and with costs.
4. It is contended by the plaintiff that he is a Class-I Civil Contractor having good reputation.
He was allotted with the contract under Water Supply Scheme to Balkundi, Mailapur and Upper Hosahalli villages in Sirguppa taluk under the composite drinking water supply scheme.
The tender was accepted in favour of the plaintiff by letter dated 22.01.2004, for a sum of Rs.2,35,67,325.41/- at 8.50%.
The plaintiff deposited a sum of Rs.2,65,000/- as earnest money as per the tender condition.

Nature of the work to be undertaken by the plaintiff is to dig a pond, construct a tank, lay a pipeline in the site shown by the defendants.
5.

It is contended that immediately after confirmation of the tender, the plaintiff commenced the contract work on the site, but he came to know that the defendants have not acquired the lands by paying compensation to the land owners before calling and finalizing the tender.
About a month after commencement of the contract work, the land owners started objecting for carrying on the work.
The plaintiff immediately brought it to the notice of the defendants.

In spite of repeated The Chief Executive Officer vs Sri Basavaraj B Sannajin on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12086022/
2 reminders in that regard, the defendants have not taken any steps to acquire their land and to free the same for carrying on the work by the plaintiff.

sentences.text: In the meantime, the land owners have written the letters dated 24.02.2006 and 18.09.2006 and objected for carrying on the work.
Even when the same was brought to the notice of the defendants, they have not taken any action.
6. It is contended that in spite of all these obstructions, the plaintiff carried on the construction work up to October, 2006 and completed the work worth Rs.1,67,12,530/-.
Due to non-acquiring of the land and clearance of objections, the plaintiff could not complete the work, in spite of extension of time granted by the defendants.
7. It is further contended that belatedly the defendants asked the Assistant commissioner, Ballary to initiated land acquisition proceedings by paying the compensation to the farmers.
Even then, the farmers were not satisfied with the award and continued their physical obstruction to the construction work.

Therefore, the plaintiff informed all these facts to the defendants and his inability to continue the work by writing the letters dated 20.11.2006, 14.02.2007, 21.08.2007 and requested the defendants to finalize the bill for the work which he had already carried on.
In spite of that, the defendants have not taken any steps.

Due to delay in carrying on the work, the cost of construction increased considerably and therefore he requested the defendants to hike the DSR rates, but the defendants have rejected such claim of the plaintiff.

8. It is contended that the plaintiff had deposited a sum of Rs.9,21,600/- as FSD (Future Security Deposit) on various dates and he is entitled to get back the same along with EMD (Earnest Money Deposit).
Due to the negligence of the defendants in calling for tender and finalizing the same without acquiring the land in question and clearing the obstructions, the plaintiff has suffered financial loss.
He has also lost the opportunity to undertake other major tender works therefore the defendants are liable to pay the damages at Rs.25,00,000/- with interest at 18% per annum.
9. It is stated that the plaintiff has issued the notice under Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure to the defendants and the same is served on them.
Defendants Nos.2 to 4 have given false and untenable reply and in the meantime, he received a letter dated 27.03.2008 intimating cancellation of the tender and calling upon for payment of penalty.

Therefore, the plaintiff sought for damages of in all Rs.24,88,600/- towards balance amount to the work completed by the plaintiff, EMD amount,
FSD amount, damages of Rs.3,00,000/- and notice charges.
10. Defendant No.3 filed his written statement denying the contentions taken by the plaintiff in the plaint.

11. It is contended that defendants allotted the tender work as per the work order dated 23.01.2004 to the plaintiff to construct the water tank and to install pipelines and other works for providing drinking water to three villages i.e. Mailapur, Uppar Hosahalli and Balkundhi of Shirguppa Taluk,
Ballari District.
The lands required were acquired by the defendants by consent of the land owners and defendants took possession of the property.
The same was handed over to the plaintiff.

sentences.text: It is also contended that the agreement was entered into between the plaintiff and the defendants on 23.01.2004 for the contract amount of Rs.2,35,67,325.41/-.
It was agreed that the plaintiff to complete the work within 2 months.
Accordingly, the defendants have handed over the site to the plaintiff on 24.01.2004 itself.
The proposed date of completion of the work was 31.03.2004.
The plaintiff started the work at the site and shown a slow progress.
On 15.03.2004 he requested the defendants to extend the period of time by 7 months i.e., from 31.03.2004 till 30.10.2004.
Even though the defendants considered the request of the plaintiff for extension of time, the plaintiff has not completed the tender work, even after expiry of the extended period.

13. It is stated that the plaintiff had written a letter dated 23.08.2006 to the Executive Engineer PRE Division, Ballary for settlement of his bills and saying no objection to give the contract to any other person, but again he had written a letter stating that he himself is ready to carry on the work if new DSR rates are approved.
The said claim of the plaintiff for revised DSR rates was rejected by the District Drinking Water and Sanitarian Committee.

sentences.text: Therefore a final notice dated 28.12.2007 was issued to the plaintiff calling upon him to complete the work.

Since the plaintiff failed to complete the work even after the deadline, the Chief Executive Officer, Zilla Panchayat, Ballary cancelled the tender on 28.02.2008 at the risk of the plaintiff and permitted for calling fresh tender for the remaining work.

14. It is contended that the Executive Engineer PRE Division, Zilla Panchayat, Ballary addressed a letter to the Deputy Commissioner, Ballary on 15.06.2004, stating that the villagers have consented for acquisition of the land for the purpose of water supply scheme to Balkundi, Mailapur and Uppar Hosahalli villages in Shirguppa Taluk, Ballary District on 23.01.2004 and there was no interference or objections by any of the land owners for execution of the work by the plaintiff.
On 13.05.2005 the Deputy commissioner directed the Assistant Commissioner to acquire the lands accordingly the Assistant commissioner initiated the acquisition proceedings.
After acquisition the compensation was dispersed to the land owners.

15. It is contended that during the pendency of the suit plaintiff had approached this Court by filing WP.No.7205/2008 against the order of the defendants canceling the contract and forfeiting EMD and FSD amount.
The said writ petition was came to be dismissed by upholding the cancellation of the tender, vide order dated 11.03.2009.
Under such circumstances, the plaintiff now cannot seek the very same relief in the suit as it operates as res judicata.
Therefore defendant No.3 prayed for dismissal of the suit with costs.

16. Defendant No.2 filed a memo adopting the written statement filed by defendant No.3.
- 10 - 17.

On the basis of these pleadings the following issues and additional issued came to be framed;
"1. Whether plaintiff proves that due to non-acquisition of land, it is not possible for him to complete work of construction of water tank within time?

Addl. Issues:
1. Whether the defendant No.3 proves that the plaintiff has failed to complete his work within 30-10-2004 as agreed by him?
2. Whether the defendant No.3 proves that the present suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable?"
18.

The plaintiff examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.69 in support of his contentions.
19.
Defendants got examined DW1 and got marked Exs.D1 to D19 in support of their contentions.

20. The Trial Court after taking into consideration all these materials on record answered issue No.1 in the affirmative, issue Nos.3 and 4 partly in the affirmative,
- 11 - additional issue No.2 in the negative, issue No.2 and additional issue No.1 were held do not survive for consideration and accordingly the suit of the plaintiff was decree in part holding that he is entitled for damages of Rs.12,00,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of suit till realization from defendant Nos.2 and 3.
21.
Being aggrieved by the same, defendant Nos.2 and 3 have preferred this appeal.

22. Heard Sri. Shivaraj V.Hiremath, learned counsel for the appellants and Sri. Anoop G.Deshpande, learned counsel for respondent No.1.
23.
Learned counsel for the appellants contended that finalizing the tender and issuance of work order is not in dispute.
It is admitted that the plaintiff was required to complete the work within two months i.e., within 31.03.2004.
Even after lapse of more than 4 years, he could not complete the work.
He was giving the lame excuse that the owners of the lands are causing obstruction.
There is absolutely no material to prove the same.

Therefore,

The same was challenged by the plaintiff before this Court by filing writ petition No.7205/2008, but the same was came to be dismissed, upholding the cancellation of the tender vide order dated 11.03.2009.
24.
Learned counsel submitted that the burden is on the plaintiff to prove that there were obstructions by the land owners for carrying on the work.
The plaintiff has not examined any witnesses to prove his contention.
The Trial Court proceeded to decree the suit only on the basis of the interested testimony of PW.1.
He further submitted that the plaintiff has not pleaded or proved any specific damages caused to him.
Under such circumstances, the Trial Court could not have decreed the suit, there is no basis for awarding the compensation at Rs.12,00,000/-.
Hence, he prays for setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court, by allowing the appeal.

25. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.1/plaintiff opposing the appeal submitted that the tender - 13 - was finalized on 23.01.2004 requiring to complete the work within 2 months i.e., on or before 31.03.2004, but the defendants have not acquired the lands that are required for construction of the tank or for laying of the pipeline.
As a result of which, the land owners objected for carrying on the work.
Even though the same was brought to the notice of the defendants, they have not taken any steps in that regard.
On 10.10.2006 the Deputy commissioner, Ballary approved the award fixing the compensation at Rs.10,947/- per acre.
Ex . P.46
discloses that the 4(1) notification was issued only on 15.06.2006.
Even thereafter the obstructions were not clear by the defendants.
Under such circumstances, the plaintiff suffered huge loss for no fault of his.

Therefore, the Trial Court rightly awarded the damages by quantifying the same at Rs.12,00,000/-.
26.

Learned counsel further submitted that the observations made by this Court in W.P.No.7205/2008 is without any materials that are placed before it, but the plaintiff has produced volumnus documents before the Civil Court which has considered the same and only thereafter - 14 - formed an opinion.
The order by this Court passed in writ petition will not act as res judicata against the plaintiff.
Therefore, he would submit that the Trial Court has taken into consideration all the materials on record and had arrived at a right conclusion.
There are no reasons to interfere with the same.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the appeal with costs.

27. Perused the materials on record including the Trial Court records.
28.

sentences.text: Whether the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court calls for interference of this Court?

29. My answer to the above point is in the negative for the following;
- 15 - REASONS 30.

It is the contention of the plaintiff that he was declared as the highest bidder to form the tank and lay the pipelines for providing drinking water to three villages i.e., Balkundi, Mailapur and Uppar Hosahalli in Shiguppa Taluk, Ballari under Composite Drinking Water Supply Scheme.
The tender was finalized and the work order was issued on 23.01.2004.
The plaintiff was required to complete the work within 2 months i.e., on 31.03.2004.
All these facts are admitted and there is no dispute about the same.

31. It is contended by the plaintiff that since the land required for construction of the tank and laying of the pipelines was not acquired by the defendants, the land owners started obstructing the work and therefore, he could not complete the work undertaken by him within the time stipulated.
He has produced Ex.P2 in support of his contention.
There is absolutely no cross-objection to PW.2 in that regard.
The Executive Engineer concerned is examined as DW.1.
He categorically stated during cross-examination that they had not obtained the written consent from the land owners for carrying on the work on their respective lands.
He admitted that there was no acquisition proceedings before calling of tender and finalizing it.
He also admits that the plaintiff has carried out the work more than what he had agreed.
Witness admits during cross-examination that the plaintiff had requested the defendants and also the land acquisition officers and the Zilla Panchayat to acquire the lands of the land owners.
He admits that the construction of the tank was completed and laying of pipelines to the water shed was only pending.
According to him, the work worth Rs.59,00,000/- was yet to be carried out by the plaintiff out of total tender amount of Rs.2.35 crores.
Witness also admits that only on 10.10.2006, the acquisition proceedings was finalized by the Deputy Commissioner.

The witness has given a fatal admission that in their anxiety to get the work complete within 31.03.2004,
they have finalized the tender, without acquiring the land in question.
He admits that the - 17 - plaintiff had informed the defendants about the objections raised by the land owners, within 15 days.

33. The evidence of PW.1, DW.1 and the documents that are placed before the Court disclose that the defendants called the tender for carrying on the work for supplying the water under the composite The Chief Executive Officer vs Sri Basavaraj B Sannajin on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12086022/
7 drinking water scheme without acquiring the land for constructing the tank or for laying the pipelines.

entities.text: Chief Executive Officer vs Sri Basavaraj B Sannajin
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even though the work order was issued on 23.01.2004 calling upon the plaintiff to complete the work on or before 31.01.2004, the 4(1) notification was issued for acquiring the land only on 13.05.2005 and the SLAO passed the award on 18.05.2006 which was approved by the DC as per Ex.P.46 on 10.10.2006.
In the meantime, there were several correspondence made by the plaintiff requesting the defendants to clear the obstructions to enable him to carryout the work.
No effort seems to have been done by the defendants in that direction.
Under such circumstances, the defendants cannot find fault with the plaintiff for not completing the work in time or atleast within the extended period of time.

The evidence of DW.1 during cross- - 18 - examination is fatal to the case of the defendants and they cannot find fault with the decreeing of the suit in favour of the plaintiff.
34.

The contention of the learned counsel for the defendants that cancellation of the tender as per Ex.P.32 was confirmed by this Court in W.P.No.7205/2008 and therefore, the same is binding on the defendants cannot be accepted.

It is only a writ proceedings where the undisputed facts are being considered by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court to form an opinion that since there is delay in completing the work, the defendants are justified in canceling the tender, but in the civil suit, the plaintiff has placed enormous materials both oral and documentary which is supported by the admissions of DW.1, which clearly go to show the negligence and inaction on the part of the defendants resulted in not completing the work in time.
None of the requirements of law to apply the principles of res judicata are focused in the present case.
Therefore, the plaintiff cannot be made as a scape goat for the lapse on the part of the defendants.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court.
It has taken into consideration all the relevant materials on record and has arrived at a right conclusion.
I do not find any reason to interfere with the same.

Hence, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following;
ORDER 1) The appeal is dismissed with costs.
2) The impugned judgment and decree dated 23.08.2011 passed in O.S.No.90/2088 by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Bellary is confirmed.
Send back the trial Court records along with a copy of this judgment.
